extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy, logic, history of science, and readers of Bacon's Novum Organum (Oxford Clarendon Press edition)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial statements for producing a single-volume annotated scholarly edition of a classical philosophical work (Bacon's Novum Organum), covering scope, annotation/printing choices, indexing, arrangement, and reproduction/microform considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the edition
rubrics_metrics.description: This Edition of the Novum Organum is intended to supply a want which... a commentary, which, besides explaining the difficulties of the work... should also present Bacon in his relations to the History of Philosophy, Logic, and Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two objects in view: (1) execute as complete an edition as possible of the author; (2) produce a work of educational value to the student of philosophy or history of thought and science. Where these objects interfere, endeavour to combine both rather than sacrifice one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: I have only annotated the Novum Organum itself, though I have thought it would be interesting to print the preliminary pieces which appeared with it on its first publication. The annotation of the minor pieces would merely have resulted in much useless repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate the main work thoroughly; exclude annotating minor/preliminary pieces to avoid repetition. Reproduce preliminary texts when interesting but avoid unnecessary annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual reproduction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of these pieces, as well as of the work itself, is re-produced after the First Edition, with the exception of several alterations in the punctuation and the frequent substitution of small for capital letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce the text after a designated edition (First Edition here) but apply consistent editorial changes such as modernizing punctuation and letter-case where appropriate; document such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational emphasis and elucidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout my Notes and Introduction I have had two objects in view... I have thought it, at least, safer to err on the side of offering too much elucidation rather than too little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer offering plentiful explanatory notes and references for students; when in doubt, provide more elucidation rather than omit potentially helpful explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed reader knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: I have assumed in my readers a certain amount of acquaintance with the history of philosophical speculation, as well as with the outlines of logic. But to readers who do not come to the study of the book with this amount of acquirement, I cannot think that an edition, worth the putting out, could be of any service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target edition toward readers with prior grounding in the field; state assumptions about prior knowledge clearly and accept that the edition may not serve complete novices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of material
rubrics_metrics.description: The arrangement of the Sections has been a matter of some difficulty... keeping apart as far as possible the expository sections from those which are mainly historical, and bringing together those which stand in any close connexion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize sections to separate expository analysis from historical material; group closely related topics together to aid coherence and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness over brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: I have studied thoroughness of treatment even at the expense of occasional prolixity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize thorough, careful exposition and comprehensive coverage, accepting some verbosity when necessary for clarity and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing conventions (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index to the Text is based on Mr. Kitchins... With the Index to the Text is incorporated the Index to the Notes. This is, for the most part, in English, as the other is, for the most part, in Latin. When a word occurs in the Notes only, it is printed in Italics; when it occurs in the Text only, or both in the Text and the Notes, it is printed in the ordinary Roman type. I have thought it desirable to draw up a separate Index to the Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine index to text with index to notes but distinguish entries typographically: italics for items only in notes; roman for items in text or both. Provide a separate index for the Introduction. Base indices on prior established indexes where useful, introducing alterations and additions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and handling of supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Those subjects which could not conveniently be treated within the compass of notes, and were still of too much importance to be omitted, I have discussed at some length in the Introduction... I have only annotated the Novum Organum itself, though I have thought it would be interesting to print the preliminary pieces which appeared with it on its first publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place extended discussions that exceed note-space into the Introduction; include important supplementary pieces in full text but limit annotation to avoid repetition and volume constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of editorial indebtedness
rubrics_metrics.description: It only remains to express my obligations to previous writers on the same subject, and to the friends who have assisted me in my work... where any explanation, reference, authority, &c., mentioned by them, had previously occurred to me or would certainly have occurred to me in the course of composition, I have not thought it necessary to make any special acknowledgment, but, where this has not been the case, I believe I have almost invariably done so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge significant prior scholarship and assistance; where ideas were independently arrived at, specific citations may be omitted, but err on the side of acknowledging when unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision transparency between editions
rubrics_metrics.description: The present edition has been carefully revised... The most important alterations or additions in this Edition occur in the passage on... (followed by a long enumerated list of pages and notes altered or added).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit list of important alterations, additions, and new notes when issuing a later edition; identify page and note locations so readers can track changes between editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity/space management constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout my Notes and Introduction I have had two objects in view— one to execute as complete an edition as possible of my author, the other to produce a work of educational value... consistent with the brevity imposed on me by the limits of a single volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing a single-volume edition, balance completeness and educational aims within space limits; make editorial choices (what to annotate, what to reprint) accordingly and state constraints in preface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microform reproduction and copyright restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright law of the United States... concerns the making of photocopies or other reproductions of copyrighted material. Under certain conditions specified in the law, libraries and archives are authorized to furnish a photocopy or other reproduction. One of these specified conditions is that the photocopy or other reproduction is not to be 'used for any purpose other than private study, scholarship, or research.' ... This institution reserves the right to refuse to accept a copy order if, in its judgement, fulfillment of the order would involve violation of the copyright law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When providing microform or photocopy reproductions, comply with copyright law and stipulate permitted uses (private study, scholarship, research); reserve right to refuse orders that may violate copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microform technical production standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical microform data: Reduction ratio; Film size; Image placement; Manufactured to film standards by Applied Image, Inc.; Filed by Research Publications, Inc., Woodbridge, CT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to established microform production standards (reduction ratio, film size, image placement) and document technical metadata and manufacturing source for archival reproductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting bibliographic irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic Irregularities in the Original Document: List volumes and pages affected; include name of institution if filming borrowed text. Page(s) missing/not available; Illegible and/or damaged page(s); Page(s) or volumes(s) misnumbered; Bound out of sequence; Page(s) or illustration(s) filmed from copy borrowed from: Other:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and report any bibliographic irregularities of the source (missing pages, damage, misnumbering, borrowed copies) in the microform/bibliographic records so users are aware of defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefatory explanation of editorial method and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: In the various sections of this Introduction... I propose to discuss a number of questions which, either from their importance or from want of space, I have found it inconvenient to treat in the notes... I have studied thoroughness of treatment even at the expense of occasional prolixity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear introductory account of editorial method, what is treated in notes vs Introduction, and justify choices about scope and depth so users understand editorial judgments and limits.
